title.narrative: Third Urban Governance and Infrastructure Improvement (Sector) Project

description.narrative: The project will strengthen urban governance and improve urban infrastructure and service delivery in 30 pourashavas (municipalities) in Bangladesh. Building upon the successful implementation of earlier phases, the project will provide investment funds to pourashavas based on their governance performance. The project will develop towns with high growth potential in an integrated and holistic way both in terms of governance and infrastructure with an aim at making them model towns of the country. In addition to the focused interventions to these towns, the project will roll out application of governance performance criteria linked with fund allocation to all class-A pourashavas in the country.

title.narrative: Loan 3142: 94% of contracts awarded and 96% disbursed as of 13 Mar 2025
Loan 3550: 92% of contracts awarded and 89% disbursed as of 13 Mar 2025
Loan 3551: 95% of contracts awarded and 96% disbursed as of 13 Mar 2025
Loan 8285: 98% of contracts awarded and 90% disbursed as of 13 Mar 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: 95,157 households have been targeted to have a new or improved access to piped water supply system. Till date 94,624 households have connections with water meters from the project. 1,30,000 households from 26 project towns will have improved solid waste management (SWM) services. Waste collection services, at least twice a week, has been ensured. Average holding tax collection efficiency in all the pourashavas was 89.15% during FY2021-2022 against the target of 85%. All the 35 pourashavas have earmarked 1% of the municipal revenue budget for the implementation of the gender action plans (GAPs), of which 94.84% (of the given 1%) have been spent during FY2021-2022.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Dec 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/39295/39295-013-39295-038-apfs-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Jan 2020: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/39295/39295-013-39295-038-iee-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Resettlement Plans | Aug 2020: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/39295/39295-013-rp-en_4.pdf
Some results are in the Safeguards Due Diligence Reports | Oct 2017: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/39295/39295-013-sddr-en_38.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Oct 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/39295/39295-013-smr-en_11.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 1. Municipal infrastructure improved and made gender and climate responsive: (a) 1,684 kilometer (km) of road and 242 km of road-side footpath have been improved or rehabilitated; (b) 613 km of drain have been built or improved; (c) 381 km water pipeline have been installed and 94,624 number individual water supply meters have been installed; (d) 252 slum improvement sub-projects are being implemented in 35 pourashavas; (e) 26 solid waste management (SWM) sites and 23 fecal sludge management (FSM) facilities are being implemented; and (g) climate issues are being considered in designing in more than 80% subprojects.
2. Improved capacity of pourashavas in urban service delivery, planning, and financial management: (a) town-level coordination committee (TLCC) and ward-level coordination committee (WLCC) were formed in 35 pourashavas with women participation achieved at 34.38%, and 40.13%, respectively; (b) urban master plans developed through gender-inclusive processes in 17 towns; (c) women and children affairs (WCA) and poverty reduction and slum improvement (PRSI) standing committees are operational in all the 35 towns and 40% women representation was ensured in each committee; (d) pourashava development plan (PDP), gender action plan (GAP), and poverty reduction action plan (PRAP) are prepared and approved in 35 pourashavas; (e) annual operation and maintenance (O&M) plan has been approved and own budget is being allocated; (f) computerized tax records and billing systems have been made functional; (g) 20 Pourashavas under Window B received subproject funding.
3. Project management and administration system in place: (a) project management unit (PMU) and project implementation units (PIUs) were established with core staff appointed at the early stage of project implementation; (b) quarterly progress reports and audit reports met ADB requirements are being submitted from Q4/2014; (c) all relevant staff oriented on gender and trained on collection and monitoring of sex-disaggregated data.
Tenders and Contracts Awarded: https://www.adb.org/projects/39295-013/main#project-tenders
